metadata.question: List the author's and publisher's name of the book published on July 10, 1997.
metadata.evidence: author's name refers to author_name; publisher's name refers to publisher_name; book published on July 10, 1997 refers to publication_date LIKE '1997-07-10'

prefix_hints.sol_1: I start from each book and connect it to its author relationships through `book_author`: `FROM book AS T1 INNER JOIN book_author AS T2 ON T1.book_id = T2.book_id`.
prefix_hints.sol_2: I join `author` through the relationship's author id so the author's name is available: `FROM book AS T1 INNER JOIN book_author AS T2 ON T1.book_id = T2.book_id INNER JOIN author AS T3 ON T3.author_id = T2.author_id`.
prefix_hints.sol_3: I also join the book's publisher to retrieve its publisher name: `FROM book AS T1 INNER JOIN book_author AS T2 ON T1.book_id = T2.book_id INNER JOIN author AS T3 ON T3.author_id = T2.author_id INNER JOIN publisher AS T4 ON T4.publisher_id = T1.publisher_id`.
prefix_hints.sol_4: I restrict the joined books to the one published on July 10, 1997: `FROM book AS T1 INNER JOIN book_author AS T2 ON T1.book_id = T2.book_id INNER JOIN author AS T3 ON T3.author_id = T2.author_id INNER JOIN publisher AS T4 ON T4.publisher_id = T1.publisher_id WHERE T1.publication_date = '1997-07-10'`.
prefix_hints.sol_5: I project the matching author's and publisher's names, completing the query: `SELECT T3.author_name, T4.publisher_name FROM book AS T1 INNER JOIN book_author AS T2 ON T1.book_id = T2.book_id INNER JOIN author AS T3 ON T3.author_id = T2.author_id INNER JOIN publisher AS T4 ON T4.publisher_id = T1.publisher_id WHERE T1.publication_date = '1997-07-10'`.

prefix_hints.sol_1: I start with the student records because their ages are the values I need to average: `FROM student AS T1`.
prefix_hints.sol_2: I connect each student to their residence record using the student id: `FROM student AS T1 JOIN lives_in AS T2 ON T1.stuid = T2.stuid`.
prefix_hints.sol_3: I then join each residence record to its dorm so the dorm name is available: `FROM student AS T1 JOIN lives_in AS T2 ON T1.stuid = T2.stuid JOIN dorm AS T3 ON T3.dormid = T2.dormid`.
prefix_hints.sol_4: I group the joined records by dorm name so the average is calculated separately for each dorm: `FROM student AS T1 JOIN lives_in AS T2 ON T1.stuid = T2.stuid JOIN dorm AS T3 ON T3.dormid = T2.dormid GROUP BY T3.dorm_name`.
prefix_hints.sol_5: Finally, I return each dorm name alongside the average age of its resident students: `SELECT avg(T1.age) ,  T3.dorm_name FROM student AS T1 JOIN lives_in AS T2 ON T1.stuid  =  T2.stuid JOIN dorm AS T3 ON T3.dormid  =  T2.dormid GROUP BY T3.dorm_name`.

answer: SELECT COUNT(T2.person_id) FROM noc_region AS T1 INNER JOIN person_region AS T2 ON T1.id = T2.region_id INNER JOIN person AS T3 ON T2.person_id = T3.id WHERE T1.region_name = 'Belgium' AND T3.gender = 'M'

metadata.question: How many males from Belgium have participated in an Olympic Games?
metadata.evidence: males refer to gender = 'M'; Belgium refers to region_name = 'Belgium';

prefix_hints.sol_1: I start with regions and link each region to its associated people through `person_region`: `FROM noc_region AS T1 INNER JOIN person_region AS T2 ON T1.id = T2.region_id`.
prefix_hints.sol_2: I join `person` so I can access each associated person's gender: `FROM noc_region AS T1 INNER JOIN person_region AS T2 ON T1.id = T2.region_id INNER JOIN person AS T3 ON T2.person_id = T3.id`.
prefix_hints.sol_3: I restrict the joined records to the Belgium region: `FROM noc_region AS T1 INNER JOIN person_region AS T2 ON T1.id = T2.region_id INNER JOIN person AS T3 ON T2.person_id = T3.id WHERE T1.region_name = 'Belgium'`.
prefix_hints.sol_4: I further restrict those Belgian participants to males: `FROM noc_region AS T1 INNER JOIN person_region AS T2 ON T1.id = T2.region_id INNER JOIN person AS T3 ON T2.person_id = T3.id WHERE T1.region_name = 'Belgium' AND T3.gender = 'M'`.
prefix_hints.sol_5: Finally, I count the matching person identifiers to return the requested number: `SELECT COUNT(T2.person_id) FROM noc_region AS T1 INNER JOIN person_region AS T2 ON T1.id = T2.region_id INNER JOIN person AS T3 ON T2.person_id = T3.id WHERE T1.region_name = 'Belgium' AND T3.gender = 'M'`.

answer: SELECT t2.title FROM publication AS t2 JOIN conference AS t1 ON t2.cid  =  t1.cid WHERE t1.name  =  "VLDB" AND t2.year  >  2000 ORDER BY t2.citation_num DESC LIMIT 1;

metadata.question: return me the paper after 2000 in VLDB conference with the most citations .

prefix_hints.sol_1: I link each publication to its conference through the shared conference id: `FROM publication AS t2 JOIN conference AS t1 ON t2.cid  =  t1.cid`.
prefix_hints.sol_2: I keep publications from the VLDB conference by matching the conference name: `FROM publication AS t2 JOIN conference AS t1 ON t2.cid  =  t1.cid WHERE t1.name  =  "VLDB"`.
prefix_hints.sol_3: I further restrict the papers to those published after 2000: `FROM publication AS t2 JOIN conference AS t1 ON t2.cid  =  t1.cid WHERE t1.name  =  "VLDB" AND t2.year  >  2000`.
prefix_hints.sol_4: I rank the qualifying papers by citation count in descending order and retain the top one: `FROM publication AS t2 JOIN conference AS t1 ON t2.cid  =  t1.cid WHERE t1.name  =  "VLDB" AND t2.year  >  2000 ORDER BY t2.citation_num DESC LIMIT 1`.
prefix_hints.sol_5: I project the title of that most-cited paper, completing the query: `SELECT t2.title FROM publication AS t2 JOIN conference AS t1 ON t2.cid  =  t1.cid WHERE t1.name  =  "VLDB" AND t2.year  >  2000 ORDER BY t2.citation_num DESC LIMIT 1;`.

Question:
Which two Asian countries share a border that is 1,782 kilometers long?
answer: SELECT T4.Country1, T4.Country2 FROM continent AS T1 INNER JOIN encompasses AS T2 ON T1.Name = T2.Continent INNER JOIN country AS T3 ON T3.Code = T2.Country INNER JOIN borders AS T4 ON T4.Country1 = T3.Code WHERE T1.Name = 'Asia' AND T4.Length = 1782

Question:
Find the net profit of the floral products which were delivered in 2021.

Evidence:
floral product refers to Product Name = 'Floral'; total net profit = SUM(Subtract(Unit Price, Unit Cost)); delivered in 2021 refers to DeliveryDate LIKE '%/21'
answer: SELECT SUM(REPLACE(T1.`Unit Price`, ',', '') - REPLACE(T1.`Unit Cost`, ',', '')) FROM `Sales Orders` AS T1 INNER JOIN Products AS T2 ON T2.ProductID = T1._ProductID WHERE T1.DeliveryDate LIKE '%/%/21' AND T2.`Product Name` = 'Floral'

Question:
For the goalie who had the most shutouts in 2010, what's his catching hand?

Evidence:
the most shutouts refers to max(SHO); shootCatch = 'L' refers to lefthand; shootCatch = 'R' refers to righthand; shootCatch = 'null' or 'empty' means this player is good at both left and right hand
answer: SELECT T1.shootCatch FROM Master AS T1 INNER JOIN Goalies AS T2 ON T1.playerID = T2.playerID WHERE T2.year = 2010 GROUP BY T2.playerID ORDER BY SUM(T2.SHO) DESC LIMIT 1

Question:
Please list the top 3 house-manufactured products with the highest average rating.

Evidence:
home manufactured refers to MakeFlag = 1; average rating = divide(sum(Rating), count(ProductReview))
answer: SELECT T2.Name FROM ProductReview AS T1 INNER JOIN Product AS T2 ON T1.ProductID = T2.ProductID WHERE T2.MakeFlag = 1 GROUP BY T2.Name ORDER BY SUM(T1.Rating) DESC LIMIT 1

metadata.question: Please list the top 3 house-manufactured products with the highest average rating.
metadata.evidence: home manufactured refers to MakeFlag = 1; average rating = divide(sum(Rating), count(ProductReview))

prefix_hints.sol_1: I join product reviews to products by `ProductID` and select each reviewed product's name: `SELECT T2.Name FROM ProductReview AS T1 INNER JOIN Product AS T2 ON T1.ProductID = T2.ProductID`.
prefix_hints.sol_2: I keep the house-manufactured products identified by `MakeFlag = 1`: `SELECT T2.Name FROM ProductReview AS T1 INNER JOIN Product AS T2 ON T1.ProductID = T2.ProductID WHERE T2.MakeFlag = 1`.
prefix_hints.sol_3: I group the review rows by product name so the ratings can be aggregated for each product: `SELECT T2.Name FROM ProductReview AS T1 INNER JOIN Product AS T2 ON T1.ProductID = T2.ProductID WHERE T2.MakeFlag = 1 GROUP BY T2.Name`.
prefix_hints.sol_4: I rank the grouped products by their summed ratings in descending order: `SELECT T2.Name FROM ProductReview AS T1 INNER JOIN Product AS T2 ON T1.ProductID = T2.ProductID WHERE T2.MakeFlag = 1 GROUP BY T2.Name ORDER BY SUM(T1.Rating) DESC`.
prefix_hints.sol_5: I return the first product in that ranking to complete the query: `SELECT T2.Name FROM ProductReview AS T1 INNER JOIN Product AS T2 ON T1.ProductID = T2.ProductID WHERE T2.MakeFlag = 1 GROUP BY T2.Name ORDER BY SUM(T1.Rating) DESC LIMIT 1`.

prefix_hints.sol_1: I start with the `male` table to identify the male people: `FROM male AS T1`.

prefix_hints.sol_3: I keep the records marked `neg`, which indicates that payment is not due: `FROM male AS T1 INNER JOIN no_payment_due AS T2 ON T1.name = T2.name WHERE T2.bool = 'neg'`.

What is the weight in pounds of the style that is produced the most by the company? If there are multiple products sharing the same weight, indicate the name of each one of them and their corresponding weights.

answer: SELECT Weight FROM Product WHERE WeightUnitMeasureCode = 'LB' GROUP BY Weight ORDER BY COUNT(Style) DESC LIMIT 1

metadata.question: What is the weight in pounds of the style that is produced the most by the company? If there are multiple products sharing the same weight, indicate the name of each one of them and their corresponding weights.
metadata.evidence: weight in pounds refers to WeightUnitMeasureCode = 'LB';

prefix_hints.sol_1: I start from `Product`, where style, weight, and weight unit are stored: `FROM Product`.
prefix_hints.sol_2: I restrict the products to weights measured in pounds using the `LB` unit code: `FROM Product WHERE WeightUnitMeasureCode = 'LB'`.
prefix_hints.sol_3: I group the matching products by weight so products sharing a weight contribute to the same result group: `FROM Product WHERE WeightUnitMeasureCode = 'LB' GROUP BY Weight`.
prefix_hints.sol_4: I select each grouped weight and order the groups by the number of non-null style values in descending order: `SELECT Weight FROM Product WHERE WeightUnitMeasureCode = 'LB' GROUP BY Weight ORDER BY COUNT(Style) DESC`.
prefix_hints.sol_5: I keep the first group to return the weight associated with the greatest style count: `SELECT Weight FROM Product WHERE WeightUnitMeasureCode = 'LB' GROUP BY Weight ORDER BY COUNT(Style) DESC LIMIT 1`.

prefix_hints.sol_5: I count distinct player IDs so a goalie appearing in multiple seasons or stints is counted once: `SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT T1.playerID) FROM Goalies AS T1 INNER JOIN Master AS T2 ON T1.playerID = T2.playerID INNER JOIN Teams AS T3 ON T1.tmID = T3.tmID AND T1.year = T3.year WHERE T3.name = 'Haileybury Hockey Club' AND T2.hofID IS NOT NULL`.

Question:
What is the product with the most profit?

Evidence:
profit = SUBTRACT(ListPrice, StandardCost);
answer: SELECT T1.ProductID FROM ProductListPriceHistory AS T1 INNER JOIN ProductCostHistory AS T2 ON T1.ProductID = T2.ProductID ORDER BY T1.ListPrice - T2.StandardCost DESC LIMIT 1

prefix_hints.sol_4: I retain only the first row in that descending profit order: `FROM ProductListPriceHistory AS T1 INNER JOIN ProductCostHistory AS T2 ON T1.ProductID = T2.ProductID ORDER BY T1.ListPrice - T2.StandardCost DESC LIMIT 1`.

Evidence:
order key refers to l_orderkey; jumbo case container refers to p_container = 'JUMBO CASE'; more than 2 parts refers to count(l_partkey) > 2
answer: SELECT T.l_orderkey FROM ( SELECT T2.l_orderkey, COUNT(T2.l_partkey) AS num FROM part AS T1 INNER JOIN lineitem AS T2 ON T1.p_partkey = T2.l_partkey WHERE T1.p_container = 'JUMBO CASE' GROUP BY T2.l_orderkey ) AS T WHERE T.num > 2

prefix_hints.sol_1: I join `part` to `lineitem` by part key so each line item is associated with its container type: `FROM part AS T1 INNER JOIN lineitem AS T2 ON T1.p_partkey = T2.l_partkey`.
prefix_hints.sol_2: I keep the line items whose parts use the jumbo case container: `FROM part AS T1 INNER JOIN lineitem AS T2 ON T1.p_partkey = T2.l_partkey WHERE T1.p_container = 'JUMBO CASE'`.
prefix_hints.sol_3: I group these line items by order key and count their part keys for each order: `SELECT T2.l_orderkey, COUNT(T2.l_partkey) AS num FROM part AS T1 INNER JOIN lineitem AS T2 ON T1.p_partkey = T2.l_partkey WHERE T1.p_container = 'JUMBO CASE' GROUP BY T2.l_orderkey`.
prefix_hints.sol_4: I use those grouped counts as a derived table and retain orders whose count is greater than 2: `FROM ( SELECT T2.l_orderkey, COUNT(T2.l_partkey) AS num FROM part AS T1 INNER JOIN lineitem AS T2 ON T1.p_partkey = T2.l_partkey WHERE T1.p_container = 'JUMBO CASE' GROUP BY T2.l_orderkey ) AS T WHERE T.num > 2`.

intermediate_turns.question: Of those, which do not speak English?

Question:
Mention the customer names and IDs which ordered total net profit of above 5000 USD through online channel.

Evidence:
IDs refers to CustomerID; total net profit of above 5000 USD refers to SUM(Subtract(Unit Price, Unit Cost)) > 5000
answer: SELECT DISTINCT `Customer Names`, CustomerID FROM ( SELECT T2.`Customer Names`, T2.CustomerID , SUM(REPLACE(T1.`Unit Price`, ',', '') - REPLACE(T1.`Unit Cost`, ',', '')) AS T FROM `Sales Orders` T1 INNER JOIN Customers T2 ON T2.CustomerID = T1._CustomerID WHERE T1.`Sales Channel` = 'Online' GROUP BY T2.CustomerID ) WHERE T > 5000

Question:
List all staff in the Shipping and Receiving department who are hired in 2009.

Evidence:
hired in 2009 refers to year(HireDate) = 2009
answer: SELECT T1.FirstName, T1.LastName FROM Person AS T1 INNER JOIN Employee AS T2 ON T1.BusinessEntityID = T2.BusinessEntityID INNER JOIN EmployeeDepartmentHistory AS T3 ON T2.BusinessEntityID = T3.BusinessEntityID INNER JOIN Department AS T4 ON T3.DepartmentID = T4.DepartmentID WHERE STRFTIME('%Y', T2.HireDate) = '2009' AND T4.Name = 'Shipping and Receiving'

prefix_hints.sol_1: I start with each person's name and connect it to their employee record through the shared business entity id: `FROM Person AS T1 INNER JOIN Employee AS T2 ON T1.BusinessEntityID = T2.BusinessEntityID`.
prefix_hints.sol_2: I continue through the employee's department history and join the corresponding department so its name is available: `FROM Person AS T1 INNER JOIN Employee AS T2 ON T1.BusinessEntityID = T2.BusinessEntityID INNER JOIN EmployeeDepartmentHistory AS T3 ON T2.BusinessEntityID = T3.BusinessEntityID INNER JOIN Department AS T4 ON T3.DepartmentID = T4.DepartmentID`.
prefix_hints.sol_3: I restrict the results to employees whose hire-date year is 2009 using SQLite's STRFTIME function: `FROM Person AS T1 INNER JOIN Employee AS T2 ON T1.BusinessEntityID = T2.BusinessEntityID INNER JOIN EmployeeDepartmentHistory AS T3 ON T2.BusinessEntityID = T3.BusinessEntityID INNER JOIN Department AS T4 ON T3.DepartmentID = T4.DepartmentID WHERE STRFTIME('%Y', T2.HireDate) = '2009'`.
prefix_hints.sol_4: I then keep only records associated with the Shipping and Receiving department: `FROM Person AS T1 INNER JOIN Employee AS T2 ON T1.BusinessEntityID = T2.BusinessEntityID INNER JOIN EmployeeDepartmentHistory AS T3 ON T2.BusinessEntityID = T3.BusinessEntityID INNER JOIN Department AS T4 ON T3.DepartmentID = T4.DepartmentID WHERE STRFTIME('%Y', T2.HireDate) = '2009' AND T4.Name = 'Shipping and Receiving'`.
prefix_hints.sol_5: Finally, I return the first and last names of the matching staff: `SELECT T1.FirstName, T1.LastName FROM Person AS T1 INNER JOIN Employee AS T2 ON T1.BusinessEntityID = T2.BusinessEntityID INNER JOIN EmployeeDepartmentHistory AS T3 ON T2.BusinessEntityID = T3.BusinessEntityID INNER JOIN Department AS T4 ON T3.DepartmentID = T4.DepartmentID WHERE STRFTIME('%Y', T2.HireDate) = '2009' AND T4.Name = 'Shipping and Receiving'`.

Question:
Which countries has the most number of airlines whose active status is 'Y'?
answer: SELECT country FROM airlines WHERE active  =  'Y' GROUP BY country ORDER BY count(*) DESC LIMIT 1

prefix_hints.sol_4: I order the country groups by their airline counts in descending order, placing the largest count first: `FROM airlines WHERE active  =  'Y' GROUP BY country ORDER BY count(*) DESC`.
prefix_hints.sol_5: I select the country and limit the result to the highest-ranked group: `SELECT country FROM airlines WHERE active  =  'Y' GROUP BY country ORDER BY count(*) DESC LIMIT 1`.
